stories.title: Food security cttee to be reconvened amid fodder concerns
stories.summary: Minister for Agriculture Martin Heydon has agreed to reconvene the National Fodder and Food Security Committee due to ongoing concerns over fodder supplies caused by the recent dry weather. That has resulted in growing concerns over fodder supplies both now and into the winter months, concerns raised at today's meeting with Minister Heydon. Minister Heydon told farmers groups that the Government will consider extra supports to address concerns over supplies of fodder, arising from the recent dry weather, as part of the upcoming Budget. The development was confirmed during a meeting today with farming groups including Teagasc, the Irish Farmers' Association, the Irish Creamery Milk Suppliers Association, Macra and a number of other farming groups.

stories.title: US securities regulator reveals long-awaited crypto rules
stories.summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission today proposed a new regulatory framework for cryptocurrency assets, the first major step under US President Donald Trump's administration to give the industry the tailored rules it has long pushed for. The SEC's proposal would exempt certain crypto companies and offerings from US securities rules, which should make it easier for crypto companies to issue tokens and raise money. The SEC's plan "seeks to provide crypto asset entrepreneurs and market participants with clear pathways to raise capital under the federal securities laws," Chairman Paul Atkins said in a statement. It would allow a one-time exemption to issue up to $5 million in crypto tokens during a four-year period.

stories.title: Tumilty eyes special World Cup day for Irish hockey
stories.summary: Ireland head coach Mark Tumilty said his players needed cool heads and real steel to beat South Africa and keep alive their hopes of progressing to the second round of the Men's Hockey World Cup in Belgium and the Netherlands. Having lost their opening Pool C match 3-1 to Australia, Ireland knew they had to beat the South Africans to realistically stay in the hunt for a top-two finish in the four-country pool. They did so thanks to a super final quarter, during which they scored three times to run out 4-1 winners. On Thursday, Ireland square up to Spain, with the winners set to join Australia in the next stage of the tournament. A draw could do Ireland thanks to their healthy goal difference.

stories.title: Kobe-mania and the Irish experiment
stories.summary: The AFL's Irish experiment nearly failed before even it really even began - and it all came down to a split-second decision in the 1987 Victorian Football League preliminary final between Melbourne and Hawthorn. The VFL was three years from morphing into the AFL and a huge crowd had gathered to watch what turned into a manic final quarter with tennis legend Pat Cash even interrupting a family holiday to attend. Melbourne missed chance after chance to kill off the Hawks’ challenge in the final minutes of the match, Simon Eishold’s incredible mis-hit hook behind long remembered by Demons fans, but it was the final play that saw it go down in infamy and left recently-recruited Dubliner Jim Stynes labelled as a laughing stock. Kept alive by Melbourne’s inefficiency, Gary Buckenara was given one last chance to win it from Hawthorn but from way out, it was a low percentage chance.

stories.title: Debut tries for Flood, Murphy as Leinster defeat Connacht
stories.summary: Debut tries from Stacey Flood and Niamh Murphy helped Leinster to overcome Connacht 36-21 for their opening Vodafone Women's Interprovincial Championship win. Having failed to pick up a point against Munster, this was a must-win game for Leinster at Energia Park, and they prevailed thanks to closing scores from Maggie Boylan and replacement Murphy. Craig Hansberry's young Connacht side led early on, and twice closed the gap to three points, but they are now a point behind second-placed Leinster, in the table, heading into the final round. Leinster's improved performance in front of their home support had them 17-14 ahead at half-time, with Boylan, Hannah Wilson, and Emma Tilly all touching down.

stories.title: Is this the second crest of Ireland's Green Wave?
stories.summary: Freelance journalist and broadcaster, writing about music and the arts. Of all the strange and surprising sights that the hallowed cobbles of Trinity College have seen over the years, a Dior fashion show might be one of the most unexpected. Thanks to Jonathan Anderson - the Creative Director of the iconic fashion brand - the university's famous Long Room will host the unveiling of the Dior Fall/Winter 2027 collection on December 4th. It’s a huge moment for Irish culture. A major fashion house has never staged a show like this on Irish soil, but the Derry-born Anderson has always been fiercely proud of his Irish roots - even wearing an Irish rugby jersey on the runway on one occasion. Perhaps this Dior-comes-to-Dublin show is his way of throwing the ladder down; he’s paying homage to his roots, but also saying to the world 'Hey, look! Not only are we great at music, writing, acting and all the rest, but the Irish have made our mark on the fashion world, too!’ It’s perhaps fortuitous that the Dior show takes place on the grounds of Trinity College, considering the much-talked-about Green Wave, or at least this most recent iteration of it, arguably began with Sally Rooney. Not only were the Mayo author’s Trinity-set novels a global phenomenon, but the TV adaptation of Normal People even had the Kardashians talking about it. It made Paul Mescal a star, spawned a plethora of literary imitators, got Gen Z talking about Irish culture and, well... the rest is history.

stories.title: Kids too young for a smartphone? We tried two alternatives
stories.summary: As a father of an eight-year-old daughter, my wife and I are beginning to loosen the safety net - just a little. In years gone by, I would have spent my summer holidays out playing from morning to evening without a care in the world until the smell of hot dinners drew us home for the night. However, times have changed, and parents want to know where their kids are when they are out of sight. This creates a dilemma. Eight seems far too young, in my opinion, for a phone that could bring the pitfalls of internet dangers, but old enough to be trusted with a certain degree of independence. So, what devices are out there, if any, that suit the bill? Well, two manufacturers of smart devices – Xplora and Karri - believe that their products can successfully fill an undoubted hole in the market for primary school children, and we were lucky enough to test them out over the past few weeks.

stories.title: Can Govt hold the line on restoration of excise on fuel?
stories.summary: The Government had hoped that as the deadline looms to begin restoring excise on fuel that the price shock at the pumps would have eased. But the continuing instability in the Middle East has shattered that expectation and the long hot summer has brought further difficulty as smaller crop yields will lead to food prices rising again. This all means that there is serious political pressure on 1 September deadline for the first of four hikes to petrol and diesel. Back in March, the Government signed off on a 'temporary' excise cut to cushion motorists, hauliers and farmers from the increases at the pumps.

stories.title: Food prices to be main driver of inflation in 2027 - ECB

Mr Lane said the rise of inflation depends on energy prices, including both oil and gas. He said "it really is an uncertain situation" but that inflation will hover at 3% for the rest of the year.

"Someday, your children will come across your disgusting and inhumane question," the White House's "Rapid Response" team said in an X post directed at Ms Holmes and linking to a video of Mr Trump's response. The Republican leader later berated Ms Holmes as "very disrespectful" as she asked a question on North Korea.

stories.summary: Todd Boehly and Mark Walter are in talks to sell their stakes in Chelsea to majority owner Clearlake Capital, according to reports. Private equity company Clearlake currently owns 61.5% of the club, with Boehly and Walter carving up the remaining shares with another investor, Hansjorg Wyss. Chelsea chairman Boehly in particular has reportedly been dissatisfied with the direction of the club recently, notably regarding recruitment, head coaches and a potential new stadium plan.

The operation is less invasive than typical heart surgery where the chest has to be opened through the breast bone. As well as being less invasive, medical experts say it also has a significantly shorter recovery time.

stories.title: Flocchini strike sends Shelbourne joint top with Athlone
stories.summary: Shelbourne held their nerve in a tense and thrilling end-to-end encounter at home to go level on points with Athlone Town at the top, with two games extra played. Bella Flocchini's first half penalty proved enough to overcome an impressive Wexford in a bruising war of attrition. Both sides came into the massive clash off the back of huge wins three days previously but showed no signs of fatigue and after a full-blooded start from both sides, the hosts broke the deadlock after just 11 minutes. Leah Doyle’s inswinging corner caused mayhem in the Wexford box, and amidst the chaos Lauren Walsh was adjudged to have hauled down Aoife Kelly at the near post.

stories.title: Offaly's All-Ireland winning captain Pádraig Horan dies
stories.summary: Pádraig Horan, who captained Offaly to their first All-Ireland hurling success in 1981, has died at the age of 76 after a long battle with illness. In a lengthy inter-county career which began at the end of the 1960s, Horan was to the fore as the Faithful famously shocked Kilkenny to win a maiden Leinster title in 1980s. Offaly had arrived, with the St Ryangh's clubman adding three more provincial crowns and another Liam MacCarthy success, in 1985, to his collection. His exploits on the field, first as a defender before moving to the full-forward berth, were also recognised when he was named on the All-Star team for '85. As a coach, he managed Offaly to win a National League title in 1991, while four years later he was at the helm when Birr landed All-Ireland senior club honours.
